commits.message:
mit-trueness-jj1.1: paint only the live window — cull settled nodes in the one loop (#49)

* mit-trueness-jj1.1: paint only the live window — cull settled nodes in the one loop

A node parked at an unchanged p (0 above it, 1 below it) had every painter
write and its barfill rewritten to the identical value every scroll frame,
forever. Cache each node's last painted p and skip when unchanged: each scene
gets exactly one final paint as it settles, then nothing.

The cull lives INSIDE the single node loop as a guard on the cached value
[LAW:single-enforcer] — no second scheduler, no IntersectionObserver. It is
provably invisible because paint(p,n) and the barfill are pure functions of p:
every painter write is absolute, never accumulated, so re-running at an
unchanged p produces identical pixels [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow].

The four post-loop seam parts (threshold/surfacing/outro/thread) are left
untouched per the ticket heads-ups — not in nodes[], cheap, and the thread is
genuinely live across the descent.

Verified in Chrome (file://, 1280x880):
- Invisibility: at 25 scroll positions spanning the full descent, the culled
  DOM is byte-identical to a forced full repaint at the same scrollY.
- Perf: held still at mid-descent for 30 frames -> 0 painter calls (was
  31 nodes x 30 = 930 identical paints); actively scrolling 30 frames ->
  only 23 paints (live window only).
- Trace: CLS 0.00 (no layout shift), no long-frame insights, console clean.

* mit-trueness-jj1.1: invalidate the paint cache on layout change

The cull assumed paint(p,n) was pure in p, but three painters read live
layout at paint time — runway (clientHeight), the DPR-aware canvas
(devicePixelRatio + clientWidth/clientHeight), and the deck (viewport
width). At a clamped p (0 above a node, 1 below it) a resize / font-load /
DPR change leaves p identical, so the cull skipped the repaint and left the
scene sized for the old viewport.

Reset n.lastP in measure() alongside the geometry cache. measure() is the
single owner of every layout-derived cache and runs only on layout-change
events (resize, load, fonts.ready via remeasure) — never per scroll frame.
So the next tick after any layout change repaints every node fresh, then
steady-state scroll culling resumes unchanged. [LAW:single-enforcer]
[LAW:one-source-of-truth]

Verified in Chrome: settled at the bottom (clamped p=1) holds at 0 paints;
a resize triggers 31 paints (full fresh repaint); settling again returns to
0 paints. Console clean.
